title: Belief update
description: Winslett's possible-models approach to updating beliefs: each old world moves to the worlds of the new information that differ from it in a minimal set of atoms, and asking whether a query holds after the update is Pi-2-complete (Eiter and Gottlob). The solutions are the pairs of an old and a new world in which the query fails; the check looks for a world of the new information that is strictly closer to the old one. relevant/1 mixes atoms of both worlds: the old values where the closer world agrees with the old one, the new values where it does not.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The old beliefs, the new information and the query. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): an old world and a new world in which the query fails.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a world was/1 that satisfies the old beliefs ...
{ was(A) } :- atom(A).
:- old(C), not was(A) : pos(C,A); was(A) : neg(C,A).
% ... and a world now/1 that satisfies the new information ...
{ now(A) } :- atom(A).
:- new(C), not now(A) : pos(C,A); now(A) : neg(C,A).
% ... in which the query clause is false.
:- query(C), pos(C,A), now(A).
:- query(C), neg(C,A), not now(A).
#show was/1.
#show now/1.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a world of the new information that is closer to the old world (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: another world alt/1 of the new information ...
{ alt(A) } :- atom(A).
:- new(C), not alt(A) : pos(C,A); alt(A) : neg(C,A).
% ... that changes fewer atoms of the old world: far(A) says the candidate's new world
% changes A, near(A) that alt/1 does. near/1 must be a proper subset of far/1.
far(A)  :- was(A), not now(A).
far(A)  :- now(A), not was(A).
near(A) :- was(A), not alt(A).
near(A) :- alt(A), not was(A).
:- near(A), not far(A).
spared(A) :- far(A), not near(A).
closer :- spared(A).
:- not closer.
#show alt/1.

% alt/1 stays closer for every candidate that
% - has the old value where alt/1 agrees with the old world;
relevant(was(A)) :- atom(A), not near(A).
% - has the new value where alt/1 changes the old world (the two new worlds agree there);
relevant(now(A)) :- near(A).
% - still changes one atom that alt/1 leaves alone (the first one will do).
relevant(now(A)) :- spared(A), not spared(B) : atom(B), B < A.

fragments.name: check_all_spared
fragments.description: The check of the variant all-spared: every atom that alt/1 spares is blamed, not only the first.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: another world alt/1 of the new information ...
{ alt(A) } :- atom(A).
:- new(C), not alt(A) : pos(C,A); alt(A) : neg(C,A).
% ... that changes fewer atoms of the old world: far(A) says the candidate's new world
% changes A, near(A) that alt/1 does. near/1 must be a proper subset of far/1.
far(A)  :- was(A), not now(A).
far(A)  :- now(A), not was(A).
near(A) :- was(A), not alt(A).
near(A) :- alt(A), not was(A).
:- near(A), not far(A).
spared(A) :- far(A), not near(A).
closer :- spared(A).
:- not closer.
#show alt/1.

% alt/1 stays closer for every candidate that
% - has the old value where alt/1 agrees with the old world;
relevant(was(A)) :- atom(A), not near(A).
% - has the new value where alt/1 changes the old world (the two new worlds agree there);
relevant(now(A)) :- near(A).
% - still changes one of the atoms that alt/1 leaves alone (all of them are named:
%   weaker than naming the first one, still sound).
relevant(now(A)) :- spared(A).

fragments.name: check_small
fragments.description: The check of the variant smallest: a closer world that changes as few atoms as possible, so the clause is short.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: another world alt/1 of the new information ...
{ alt(A) } :- atom(A).
:- new(C), not alt(A) : pos(C,A); alt(A) : neg(C,A).
% ... that changes fewer atoms of the old world: far(A) says the candidate's new world
% changes A, near(A) that alt/1 does. near/1 must be a proper subset of far/1.
far(A)  :- was(A), not now(A).
far(A)  :- now(A), not was(A).
near(A) :- was(A), not alt(A).
near(A) :- alt(A), not was(A).
:- near(A), not far(A).
spared(A) :- far(A), not near(A).
closer :- spared(A).
:- not closer.
#show alt/1.
% The smallest refinement (variant smallest): as few changed atoms as possible.
#minimize { 1,A : near(A) }.

% alt/1 stays closer for every candidate that
% - has the old value where alt/1 agrees with the old world;
relevant(was(A)) :- atom(A), not near(A).
% - has the new value where alt/1 changes the old world (the two new worlds agree there);
relevant(now(A)) :- near(A).
% - still changes one atom that alt/1 leaves alone (the first one will do).
relevant(now(A)) :- spared(A), not spared(B) : atom(B), B < A.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% Beliefs over the atoms a..g, in clause form: pos(C,A) / neg(C,A) are the literals
% of clause C.
atom(a;b;c;d;e;f;g).
% What was believed before the change:
neg(1,b). pos(1,c). neg(1,f).         % ~b | c | ~f
neg(2,d). neg(2,g).                   % ~d | ~g
pos(3,c). pos(3,d).                   % c | d
old(1..3).
% What is learnt about the world after the change:
pos(4,b). pos(4,c).                   % b | c
pos(5,a). pos(5,f).                   % a | f
neg(6,b). neg(6,e).                   % ~b | ~e
neg(7,a). pos(7,g).                   % ~a | g
new(4..7).
% The query: does this clause hold after the update?
pos(8,c). pos(8,f).                   % c | f
query(8).

% a was believed, and the new information speaks only about b, c, d and e. Minimal change
% never touches a: the query a holds after the update.
atom(a;b;c;d;e).
pos(1,a). old(1).                     % a
neg(2,b). neg(2,c). old(2).           % ~b | ~c
pos(3,d). pos(3,e). old(3).           % d | e
pos(4,b). pos(4,c). new(4).           % b | c
neg(5,d). pos(5,b). new(5).           % ~d | b
pos(6,a). query(6).                   % a

% Door (d), window (w) and hatch (h) were closed; the fan (f) may have been on or off.
% Now one of the three is open, and an open hatch means the fan runs. Does the door stay
% closed? Not after every minimal change: opening only the door is minimal.
atom(d;w;h;f).
neg(1,d). old(1).                     % ~d
neg(2,w). old(2).                     % ~w
neg(3,h). old(3).                     % ~h
pos(4,d). pos(4,w). pos(4,h). new(4). % d | w | h
neg(5,h). pos(5,f). new(5).           % ~h | f
neg(6,d). query(6).                   % ~d

% It was believed that the light (c) is on if the switch (a) is on; now the switch is
% on. Does the light come on? Not by minimal change: a world with switch and light off
% becomes one with only the switch on.
atom(a;c).
neg(1,a). pos(1,c). old(1).           % ~a | c
pos(2,a). new(2).                     % a
pos(3,c). query(3).                   % c

generators.name: bu-random
generators.description: Random beliefs in clause form: n atoms, o old clauses, w new clauses and a query clause; each atom occurs in a clause positively or negatively with probability p/1000 each.
generators.text:
% bu-random: atoms 1..n; clauses 1..o are the old beliefs, the next w the new information
% and the last one the query. An atom occurs in a clause positively or negatively with
% probability p/1000 each; every clause has a literal.
atom(1..n).
old(1..o).
new(o+1..o+w).
query(o+w+1).
sign(C,A,@weighted((1000-2*p, p, p), C, A)) :- C = 1..o+w+1, atom(A).
pos(C,A) :- sign(C,A,2).
neg(C,A) :- sign(C,A,3).
used(C) :- sign(C,A,S), S > 1.
:- C = 1..o+w+1, not used(C).
#show atom/1.  #show old/1.  #show new/1.  #show query/1.  #show pos/2.  #show neg/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: each refuted candidate is ruled out on its own.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Shape 2: explicit solves of A; each solution is blocked by A.add.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three counterexamples per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The smallest refinement: an optimal counterexample (check_small minimises the
# atoms that relevant/1 blames), so its clause is as short as possible.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

library.summary: Updating beliefs by minimal change (possible-models approach): old and new worlds that refute a query, checked against closer worlds (7 atoms, 8 solutions).
